clue.text: Company without a name accepts lawful partnership

indicators.note: the shortened company takes the lawful word into its middle, as a host accepts a guest
without means these letters are dropped from the word for company

parts.note: the word itself, spelt out in full
licit means permitted by law

explanation.surface: A firm that has lost its name takes on a perfectly legal business partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company without a name' looks like an anonymous firm; it is the word itself losing two letters, and 'accepts' puts the lawful word inside what remains, COMPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Complicity is involvement with others in a wrongdoing, a partnership in crime.

clue.text: Attractive, off-side shot over point

parts.note: in cricket the cut is a stroke played to the off side
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A batsman's attractive stroke through the off side, beyond the fielder at point.
explanation.walkthrough: Point is also a cricket fielding position, which the surface leans on; here it is a compass point. A cut is a cricket stroke played square on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute is a near synonym for pretty or appealing.

clue.text: Instrument used by African wood-tappers?

parts.note: wood-tappers sounds like woodpeckers or lumberjacks, but the players strike wooden bars with mallets on a xylophone-like instrument of African origin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tool for tapping trees; the tapping is musical, on wooden keys.
explanation.definitionFit: The marimba is a wooden-keyed percussion instrument that came to the Americas from Africa.

clue.text: Daft headline turns out to be vitally important

indicators.note: turns out signals that the letters of the two words get rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A silly newspaper headline proves to be of crucial importance after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges the twelve letters of DAFT HEADLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter of the utmost seriousness is described as a matter of survival or extinction.

clue.text: Flowery pieces from Newcastle, for example

definitions.meaning: pieces of china from a Shropshire factory known for flower-decorated porcelain
Newcastle upon Tyne was a harbour famous for shipping coal

explanation.surface: Decorated floral items that come from a city in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Coalport is an English make of porcelain, often painted with flowers; Newcastle was the classic harbour for shipping coal, hence 'coals to Newcastle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coalport is a brand of fine bone china; Newcastle is the archetypal harbour exporting coal.

clue.text: Number of tumblers in bistro up-ended

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A tray of drinking glasses is knocked over in a little restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-ended' is not a reversal signal here: the letters run forwards across bistrO UP Ended. Tumblers are acrobats, not glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of performers, here acrobats.

clue.text: Capital taken from racecourse tax, formerly

indicators.note: the capital, or head letter, of the racecourse name is removed, beheading it

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: Money is raised from a racecourse by a levy of olden times.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is the royal racecourse west of London. Capital here means the capital letter at its head, A, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot was a medieval municipal levy, surviving in the phrase scot-free.

clue.text: Start of Christmas rush? Correct!

indicators.note: start of picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to hasten is to rush

explanation.surface: The beginning of the festive shopping frenzy, and someone confirms it.
explanation.walkthrough: Correct is the verb, to punish or rebuke, not the adjective it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to discipline or rebuke someone.

clue.text: Tremendous night out around Neath

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes around the other piece
out signals that the letters of night are put out of their order

parts.note: neath is a poetic form of beneath, so under

explanation.surface: A wonderful evening out on the town in the Welsh town of Neath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns the letters into THING. Neath is also a town in South Wales, which the surface uses; here it is the poetic 'beneath'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thundering is an informal intensifier meaning very great.

clue.text: Turn out to arrest of wrongdoer

indicators.note: turn out tells us these letters are to be turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go out and arrest a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' rearranges the letters of TO ARREST OF. The answer is a legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a tortfeasor is someone who commits a civil wrong.

clue.text: Retiring cricketer, university opener, is ruled out

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the word for the cricketer is read in reverse

parts.note: a bat is a batsman

indicators.note: opener picks the first letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A cricketer retires, a university batsman opens, and he is given out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' reverses BAT to TAB, and 'opener' gives U from university.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, meaning forbidden.

clue.text: One airs things for three schools when they break up

indicators.note: break up signals that the letters of three schools come apart and reform

explanation.surface: Something to dry washing for three schools when term ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Schools 'break up' for the holidays, but here the phrase rearranges THREE SCHOOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse is a frame on which laundry is hung to dry.

clue.text: Was she announced as the nightly-engaged girl?

definitions.text: Was she announced as the nightly-engaged girl?

parts.words: Was she announced as the nightly-engaged girl?
parts.note: in old military signalling PM was spoken as Pip followed by a girl's name, so the girl is paired nightly with Pip in announcing evening times

explanation.walkthrough: Old signallers' alphabet said M as a girl's name: AM was 'Ack' plus her, PM 'Pip' plus her, so after noon she is engaged to Pip.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old phonetic alphabet the letter M was spoken as this name, as in pip-emma for afternoon.

clue.text: Unfinished work given coat of silver? That's settled!

indicators.note: the shortened work is given a covering, placed inside the coating word

parts.note: plated means given a thin coat of silver

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: opus is Latin for a work, especially of music

explanation.surface: An incomplete piece gets a silver finish, and the matter is resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the S, and 'given' puts the remainder inside the plating word, the coat. Settled means inhabited, not resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: A populated place is one that has been settled by inhabitants.

clue.text: One up at Badminton?

parts.note: suggests a player leading at shuttlecock, but Badminton is the Gloucestershire estate hosting horse trials, where riders are up in the saddle

explanation.walkthrough: Badminton Horse Trials are held at Badminton House in Gloucestershire, England; one up means mounted.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse rider is someone mounted, which is what being up at the trials means.

clue.text: Dilemma when, in France, a line is shortened

parts.note: quand is French for when
railway is the line, cut short to its abbreviation RY

explanation.surface: In France, a queue is cut, causing a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is the usual abbreviation for railway, a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a state of perplexity over what to do.

clue.text: One doing penance agreed by the King

parts.note: at one means in agreement
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A penitent's offering is accepted by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: R is Rex, king, as on British coins and documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes amends for a sin is making atonement.

clue.text: Standard sort of saint and follower

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: sort of hints that the letters of saint are sorted into another order

explanation.surface: A conventional kind of holy figure with a disciple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the saint's letters into TISAN. Standard looks like a banner, but it is the golfer's norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a committed supporter of a cause or party.

clue.text: Note composite early festival

parts.note: E is a musical note
the aster is a plant of the composite, daisy, family

explanation.surface: A musical piece put together for a festival early in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite is a botanical family name (daisies and asters), not 'made of parts'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian spring feast comes early in the calendar year.

clue.text: Observe fine porcelain appearance?

parts.note: to see is to observe
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain from the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: Take a look at a delicate Chinese vase's appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeming as a noun means outward show, how something looks.

clue.text: The world organised to admit one sedative drug?

parts.note: vale, as in vale of tears, is a poetic term for this world

indicators.note: the word for organised lets the numeral in, holding it inside

parts.note: ran means managed or organised
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Everyone is arranged to take a calming medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to admit' gives RIAN. Vale for the world is a poetic usage, as in 'this vale of tears'.
explanation.definitionFit: Valerian root is a herbal remedy used as a sedative.

clue.text: Guts needed for fashionable parties

parts.note: in means fashionable
sides are parties in a dispute

explanation.surface: Courage is required for trendy social gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: Guts looks like courage but means entrails; parties are sides in a dispute, not gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: The innards or entrails of a body are its internal organs.

clue.text: Evacuate city area enveloped by fog

indicators.note: enveloped by means the city letters are wrapped inside the fog word

parts.note: damp means moisture or mist
EC is the postcode area for the City of London

explanation.surface: Leave the town district when a mist engulfs it.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the postal district of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly, to quit a place.

clue.text: Handling medicine with care

definitions.meaning: the way something or someone is dealt with
medical attention given to a patient

explanation.definitionFit: Treatment means both the manner of dealing with something and medical care given to the sick.

clue.text: Army entertainer …

definitions.meaning: someone who receives guests at a party

explanation.definitionFit: Host means a great multitude of soldiers, and also one who receives and entertains guests.

clue.text: Impassioned lament?

definitions.meaning: to wail in grief for the dead, an Irish mourning cry

explanation.definitionFit: Keen means eager and enthusiastic, and also to wail in mourning.

clue.text: … one twice getting the bird

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat

explanation.surface: Someone is booed off stage two times over.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting the bird means being booed, which the surface plays on; here the bird is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-billed wading bird.

clue.text: Loopy game for kids in New Orleans?

definitions.text: Loopy game for kids in New Orleans?

parts.words: Loopy game for kids in New Orleans?
parts.note: a string game of loops, read in a second sense: jazz players are called cats and New Orleans is called the birthplace of jazz

explanation.walkthrough: New Orleans is known as the cradle of jazz, and jazz musicians are 'cats', so it is the jazzmen's birthplace as well as a children's string game.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's cradle is a children's game of making patterns with a loop of string between the fingers.

clue.text: Near dark (not quite)

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: night is the time of dark

explanation.surface: It is nearly nightfall, but not completely dark yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter, T, from NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for close by.

clue.text: The game should be fair at this time of year

definitions.text: The game should be fair at this time of year

parts.words: The game should be fair at this time of year
parts.note: reads like sportsmanship, but game here means animals hunted, which are fair targets once the hunting period begins

explanation.walkthrough: Game means quarry and fair means a legitimate target, not a sporting contest played fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: The period when hunting a particular animal is legally permitted.
